Share on X Telegram ‏The Ondo State Deputy Governor, Dr Olayide Adelami, has urged Nigerians to re-elect President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election, describing another four-year term for the president as an opportunity to consolidate ongoing economic reforms and sustain national development.
Adelami said the Tinubu administration had taken bold steps towards reforming the economy, arguing that the policies required more time to deliver lasting benefits to Nigerians.
According to a statement issued on Saturday by his spokesman, John Akinduro, the deputy governor made the appeal at a presidential campaign rally in Owo, headquarters of Owo Local Government Area of Ondo State.
He said the reforms introduced by the Federal Government were necessary to establish a strong foundation for inclusive and sustainable development, urging Nigerians to support continuity rather than what he described as retrogression.
He said, “No president has done what Asiwaju (Tinubu) has done with the economy, and it is the best thing to do in the interest of Nigeria and Nigerians.
“The reforms are already yielding good results. Currently, every state in the country has increased wages and is paying regularly. Pensioners and civil servants are receiving their monthly pay as and when due, states now have more funds for infrastructural development.”
The deputy governor also commended the people of Owo for their continued support for Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa and urged them to sustain their backing for the All Progressives Congress ahead of the forthcoming elections.
He described Aiyedatiwa as a leader who assumed office at a critical period and had demonstrated the capacity to provide exemplary leadership and direction for the state.
Adelami further called on registered voters in Owo and neighbouring communities to collect and protect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), while mobilising support for the ruling party.
Earlier, the Director-General of the Ondo State APC Presidential Campaign Council, Victor Olabimtan, urged residents of Ose and Owo local government areas to secure at least 75 per cent of registered voters’ support for the party in the January 16 election.
He also called on party members to mobilise support for all APC candidates ahead of the February 6, 2027, House of Assembly election, describing the poll as crucial to the party’s electoral fortunes.
